text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Liberals turn sights on opposition leader: Prime minister attacks Reform Party leader Preston Manning.
- Record low lending rates hint at Canadian economic rebound.
- Bre-X finds key ally in Indonesia.
- Canadian provincial premiers tell prime minister not to offload native concerns on provinces.
- Quebec separatist party changes sovereignty option: Quebec government is more right-wing, less impatient a year after referendum.
- Bre-X gets Indonesian ally: Strikes deal with company controlled by President Suharto's eldest son in a bid to end legal entanglements.
- Canadian oil patch thrives on gush of cash flow: High crude prices spur drilling activity.
- Canadian industrialist Frank Stronach sees pay slashed to $20.4 million: Chief of Magna International Inc. takes more than 50 percent pay cut.
- The downside of low Canadian interest rates: Meagre returns are taking their toll on retirees and investors.
- Bre-X finds powerful friend: Shares rise strongly as junior Canadian mining company strikes a deal on its gold property with a group controlled by the son of Indonesian President Suharto.
- Canadian rates keep sliding and federal government keeps winning.
